chain.label: High density altitude at cliff/accident-site elevations
chain.trigger: high-ambient temperatures and resultant high-density altitude

chain.label: Precipitous escarpment terrain along route with no suitable landing options nearby
chain.trigger: precipitous and rugged canyon topography with few locations that would be suitable for emergency autorotations

chain.label: 5-10 knot tailwind on the reversed heading toward the cliff
chain.trigger: winds from 3,000 to 6,000 feet were from the west at 5 to 10 knots

chain.label: Pilot's habitual low-altitude, high-speed dive maneuver at the cliff edge
chain.trigger: he preferred to cross the cliff edge at low altitude and high speed... he would then enter a rapid descent by lowering the collective and nosing the helicopter over into a dive

chain.label: Pilot slowed and reversed heading 180 degrees back toward the cliff after crossing it
chain.trigger: the helicopter reduced forward airspeed and reversed its heading

caused_by.evidence: this scenario assumes that the pilot elected to execute a descending 180o turn with an abrupt slowing of forward speed back toward the cliff after crossing the face of the Grand Wash Cliffs
any tailwind component would significantly decrease the hover and vertical climb performance capabilities of the helicopter

chain.label: Unrecoverable high rate of descent given the helicopter's degraded performance margin
chain.trigger: resulting in a high rate of descent from which the pilot was unable to recover prior to ground impact

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to maneuver the helicopter in a flight regime, and in a high density altitude environment, which significantly decreased the helicopter's performance capability

the available power margin at the accident site altitude translates into a helicopter vertical climb capability from a hover of only 421 fpm at best. If the helicopter were descending vertically (or nearly so) at a greater rate, the pilot could not arrest the descent
the high rate of descent occurred in proximity to precipitous terrain, which effectively limited remedial options available

chain.label: Collision with terrain
chain.trigger: collided with terrain during an uncontrolled descent about 4 miles east of Meadview, Arizona

caused_by.evidence: collided with terrain during an uncontrolled descent

chain.label: Fatal and serious injuries to occupants
chain.trigger: The pilot and five passengers were killed, and the remaining passenger sustained serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: The pilot and five passengers were killed, and the remaining passenger sustained serious injuries
